newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF, BOJ forming plan to help NCB - paper.
newsitem.headline: MOF, BOJ forming plan to help NCB - paper.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) and the Bank of Japan (BOJ) have started formulating a plan to boost the capital of troubled Nippon Credit Bank Ltd by 300 billion yen, a Japanese business daily said on Friday.
Nihon Keizai Shimbun said the financial authorities had already started asking major banks and life insurance companies to cooperate with them to help NCB.
The ministry and the BOJ were not immediately available for comment.
NCB's capital is seen falling as a result of an expected write-off of problem loans, the paper said.

The authorities, which had already expressed full support for NCB, will use 80 billion to 90 billion yen of BOJ funds that were originally set aside to deal with bad loans at "jusen" mortgage firms to help boost NCB's capital, the paper said. They are also asking major Japanese banks for financial support totalling 70 billion yen and asking life insurers to extend subordinated loans to NCB that could total 150 billion yen, the paper said.
In addition they are asking major Japanese banks and life insurers for a total of about 220 billion yen in support, the paper said.
Bank sources said on Thursday that MOF had asked commercial banks to help NCB in its efforts at restructuring.
They said a senior MOF official visited bank offices on Thursday asking them to buy new shares to be issued by NCB in order to boost the ailing bank's capital.
